CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the effectiveness of recent medication adjustments for anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents today for a follow-up appointment, expressing cautious optimism regarding his treatment regimen. Since the last visit, he reports a slight improvement in his sleep patterns, achieving approximately 8 hours of sleep per night on average. He notes that while sleep initiation remains a challenge, the recent increase in trazodone to 75 mg nightly has contributed positively to reducing nocturnal awakenings. However, he continues to experience emotional distress related to his sleep issues, which he describes as frustrating.
Despite the improvements in sleep, Mr. Smith reports that fatigue persists, particularly during workdays when project demands are high. He acknowledges that the combination of sleep disturbances and occupational stressors contributes significantly to his overall fatigue. His headache frequency has decreased slightly, now occurring three times per week, with intensity averaging 4 on a scale of 10. He has continued to take amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly, which he feels has provided some relief, but he still relies on ibuprofen occasionally for breakthrough headaches.
Mr. Smith remains committed to his holistic treatment plan, attending acupuncture sessions twice weekly and practicing yoga regularly. He reports that mindfulness strategies and relaxation techniques have been beneficial, particularly during stressful work periods. His anxiety levels appear stable, with no significant fluctuations reported.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where project deadlines remain a significant source of stress. He maintains an active lifestyle, regularly attending yoga classes and practicing meditation. He abstains from alcohol and adheres to a plant-based diet, with occasional indulgences in processed foods during particularly stressful periods.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Improved sleep initiation; anxiety remains manageable with therapy and medication; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Decreased headache frequency; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 68 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert and oriented, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce tapering of lorazepam use as needed. Schedule follow-up therapy sessions to further enhance coping strategies. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg; maintain melatonin at 10 mg; continue CBT-I strategies and monitor sleep patterns closely. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly; if headache frequency increases or intensity worsens, consider topiramate for preventive therapy at the next follow-up. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Emphasize the importance of physical activity and mindfulness practices. Continue to monitor dietary habits and consider a nutritionist referral if fatigue persists.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-05-01 to assess ongoing symptoms, evaluate treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to reach out sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
